   5.7-magnitude quake strikes central Japan, at least 20 injured in Aichi prefecture

 Published   Nov 08, 2026, 06:34 AM

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise A 5.7-magnitude quake struck central Japan at 1.04am on Nov 8, with the epicentre in western Shizuoka at about 40km depth.
 At least 20 people were injured in Aichi prefecture, and the Japan Meteorological Agency recorded upper 5 intensity in Chita and lower 5 in nearby areas.
 The government set up a liaison office to respond, and officials said there was no tsunami risk.
 AI generated
 AICHI - An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.7 struck central Japan early on Nov 8, leaving at least 20 people injured in Aichi prefecture, authorities said.
 The 1.04am temblor originated in the western part of Shizuoka prefecture at a depth of about 40km, and registered upper 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale in Chita, Aichi prefecture, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
 An intensity of lower 5 was recorded in parts of Aichi, Nagano and Gifu prefectures.
 The government set up a liaison office to respond to the quake.
 The agency said the quake posed no risk of tsunami. KYODO NEWS
